title: Transactional KV reserve with hedged fallback and retry quorum
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Background: production telemetry shows rare but high-cost P99 OOM cascades when bursty long-context requests coincide with cold KV states. Existing soft-eviction + model-fallback approaches reduce incidents but still cause multi-request retries and degraded latency. Goal: implement a transactional reservation layer for KV allocations at request admission time that coordinates hedged fallback launches and a quorum-based retry policy to avoid duplicate heavy work and to provide deterministic graceful degradation.

Scope: implement a lightweight KV-reservation protocol in the serving admission path, integrate with continuous-batching controller, and wire hedged fallback orchestration that can: 1) atomically reserve a bounded KV ticket for a request or batch-window, 2) fall back to a smaller-model variant or truncated-context path when reservation fails, and 3) execute hedged retries under a retry-quorum (N-of-M) rule to limit overload storms.

Success criteria / metrics: reduce end-to-end P99 latency regression on OOM windows by 45% vs baseline; reduce OOM-caused request retries by 70%; maintain per-tenant SLO (95th token latency) within 1.2x during burst events. Add instrumentation: reservation_acquired, reservation_rejected_reason, hedged_fallback_triggered, quorum_retry_decision.

Design highlights and trade-offs: transactional reservations are implemented as a low-latency in-memory sequencer per-GPU node with epoch-based expiry (default 300ms). This minimizes cross-node coordination (no distributed consensus) at the cost of possible over-reservation at edge cases; over-reservation is mitigated by fast expiry and admission backpressure. Hedged fallback launches first try a micro-quantized variant on the same node (fast), then a smaller-architecture model in the model-ladder as a secondary fallback. The retry-quorum defaults to 1-of-2 (one initial attempt + one hedged) to cap duplicate heavy work while preserving low-latency wins.

API & Config: new admission config block: {"kv_reservation_enabled": true, "reservation_timeout_ms": 300, "hedge_policy": "micro-quant-first", "quorum": "1_of_2"}. Exposed via runtime-1.22 feature flag and per-customer override.

Rollout plan: 1) internal staging with synthetic burst tests, 2) canary on low-traffic shard (10% traffic) + compare reservation metrics, 3) progressive ramp to 50% then 100% with automatic rollback trigger if OOM ratio increases >10%.

Dependencies: batch-admission-slice API (ENG-43058), adaptive-kv-compression work (ENG-52310) for memory headroom, and console tracing hooks for per-request reservation traces.

Testing: unit tests for sequencer expiry, integration tests simulating simultaneous reservation attempts, chaos test that injects reservation node failures and verifies fallback behavior, and ML-eval-like prompt set to verify output fidelity under fallback.

SLO and cost considerations: hedged fallbacks increase transient compute but reduce tail retries; we will monitor cost-per-successful-response. If cost delta > 12% we will tune quorum to 1_of_1 for non-critical tiers.
comments: 2025-02-19 — Initial spike: prototyped sequencer in go-serving; measured median reservation latency 120us and 95th 380us on g4dn-like node.
2025-02-21 — Design review with runtime and infra teams. Decision: use node-local sequencer (avoid cross-node RPC) + epoch expiry. Action: Maya to write integration test harness.
2025-02-24 — PM feedback (Ava Patel): prefer canary gating by customer tier (dev/test vs production) and explicit opt-in for private deployments. Added config override and doc note.

2025-02-28 — Engineering safety review: flagged risk that sequencer expiry set too low could cause false negatives under GC pauses. Agreed to add jittered retry and observability for expiry_count metric.

2025-03-03 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1542 (kv-reserve controller + unit tests). Running CI; integration tests failing intermittently due to race in epoch cleanup — assigned to Jose Alvarez to fix.

2025-03-05 — QA report: synthetic load test (1000 concurrent long-context requests) shows OOM-retry rate reduced from 2.8% to 0.6% in staging with hedged fallback enabled. Observability gaps: need a dashboard for reservation_rejected_reason counts.
